wastewater is pumped into rectangular primary sedimentation basins to remove floatable and settleable material.

Primary effluent is gravity-fed to 440 acres of mechanically aerated Oxidation Ponds, where organic matter and ammonia are degraded by aerobic and anaerobic bacteria. Nitrification and denitrification in the ponds...
Treated pond effluent is pumped to Fixed Growth Reactors (FGRs) (i.e., trickling filters) that provide additional nitrification of ammonia.
FGR effluent is conveyed to the Dissolved Air Flotation Tanks (DAFTs), where compressed air and polymer are injected to coagulate, flocculate, and remove biological solids (algae and bacteria)...
the wastewater undergoes filtration through four parallel dual media filters... The settled solids from the filter backwash water are pumped back to the oxidation ponds.

Sodium hypochlorite is metered into the filtered effluent at the beginning of four serpentine chlorine contact tanks to generate a chlorine residual... As the effluent leaves the contact tanks, sodium bisulfite is added as needed to neutralize the hypochlorite.

The Discharger pumps sludge produced in the primary sedimentation basins to primary anaerobic digesters. Generally, the Discharger operates secondary digesters in series to stabilize and thicken the biosolids...
